correctness.rationale: The intensity normalization follows from the analytic covariance and Edelman–Kostlan formula; differentiating the Gaussian-smoothed PSD yields \(\rho=m\prime=4\pi\operatorname{Var}(X)\). The covariance identity proves sign, Gaussian localization proves the two subquadratic coefficients, exact error-function asymptotics prove the \(\beta=1\) coefficient, and Laplace concentration at the unique positive saddle proves the superquadratic coefficient. The exact transport identity proves deficit balance. Numerical checks were run as corroboration, not extrapolation.

value.rationale: The explicit five-regime zero-intensity diagnostic, sharp transition from eventual superwhite tail intensity to global subwhite intensity at \(\beta=1\), and exact total-deficit cancellation at \(\beta<1\) provide an informative complete invariant for a standard continuously parametrized spectrum. This is more than numerical evaluation of a known general formula; it gives sharp constants and a new global compensation identity. Scope is restricted to population intensities.
